doc.headline: No price was set on quality: Atlas-M costs {cost.gap.atlas-m.atlas-l.per_1k|abs} less per 1,000 conversations than Atlas-L and trails it only on overall quality; Brisk-S is cheapest but slips on safety checks.
doc.lede: Each step up the price frontier buys overall quality at a rising price per point, and no check separates Atlas-M from Atlas-L. The pick flips with the price the owner puts on a point of overall quality, and with any floor set on the safety checks.

caveats.material_if: It moves the pick, not the figures: with no bar, floor or price per point declared, the option follows whatever price the owner sets, so the report prices the trade and leaves the call to the concierge owner.

Only if the unstated judge of the pass/fail checks reads Brisk-S or Open-70B more harshly than the Atlas models; the price frontier itself rests on overall quality, whose judge is calibrated on {judged.overall.calibration_ratings} human ratings at {judged.overall.agreement} agreement.

Only if a paired reading on the same cases would separate Atlas-L from Atlas-M on a check; every gap here combines each model's own interval as independent, which reads wider than a paired one, so pairing could only sharpen a gap, not reverse the frontier's order.

Only if a fresh run reads Atlas-L's lead over Atlas-M lower than its {price.atlas-m.atlas-l.overall.gain} pooled points (unpaired interval {price.atlas-m.atlas-l.overall.gain_interval_unpaired}); a smaller lead raises the price of each point bought on to Atlas-L and favours Atlas-M.

caveats.label: Cost routing unknown
caveats.material_if: Only if another provider serving any of these models would reorder their costs; the run names no provider for any model, so each cost is this run's routing, not the model's own.

decision.text: Atlas-L leads Atlas-M by {price.atlas-m.atlas-l.overall.gain} points of overall quality, pooled over traffic, and costs {cost.gap.atlas-m.atlas-l.per_1k|abs} more per 1,000 conversations. Atlas-M leads Brisk-S by {price.brisk-s.atlas-m.overall.gain} points, costs {cost.gap.brisk-s.atlas-m.per_1k|abs} more, and leads it on the safety checks too.

Brisk-S is the best buy if a point of overall quality is worth less than somewhere from {price.brisk-s.atlas-m.overall.per_point_low_unpaired} to {price.brisk-s.atlas-m.overall.per_point_high_unpaired} per 1,000 conversations; Atlas-L if it is worth more than somewhere from {price.atlas-m.atlas-l.overall.per_point_low_unpaired} to {price.atlas-m.atlas-l.overall.per_point_high_unpaired}; Atlas-M in between. A price inside either band is not settled by this run.

Ours, not a declared rule: Atlas-M, for any price per point in the middle band. No pass/fail check tells it apart from Atlas-L, while Brisk-S's saving comes with drops on declining to speculate and confirming before account changes.

Open-70B is off the price frontier on point estimates only: its pooled lead over Brisk-S is {price.brisk-s.open-70b.overall.gain} points, interval {price.brisk-s.open-70b.overall.gain_interval_unpaired}, so a point bought on to it could cost as little as {price.brisk-s.open-70b.overall.per_point_low_unpaired}, inside Brisk-S's band. What clearly counts against it: it confirms before account changes {compare.atlas-m.open-70b.confirms.task.trouble.difference|abs} points less often than Atlas-M, and trails Atlas-M on overall quality in every task but persona small talk.

No line was declared, so there is no weakest margin to watch. Speculation bait carries {task.specul.share} of traffic: its decline rates say what each model does when baited, not what live traffic meets. Every cost is this run's provider routing, which is unnamed.
The concierge owner declares a price per point of overall quality, or a floor on declining to speculate and confirming before account changes; either turns the trade into a call.

claims.text: Each step up the price frontier buys overall quality at a rising price: a point costs {price.brisk-s.atlas-m.overall.per_point} per 1,000 conversations from Brisk-S to Atlas-M, and {price.atlas-m.atlas-l.overall.per_point} from Atlas-M on to Atlas-L.

evidence.caption: Price per point of overall quality at each step of the frontier, per 1,000 conversations, with unpaired intervals; on point estimates Open-70B is never the best buy, though its interval against Brisk-S leaves that open.

claims.text: Brisk-S's saving comes with drops on the safety checks: it declines to speculate {compare.atlas-m.brisk-s.declines.task.specul.difference|abs} points less often than Atlas-M, and Open-70B also falls short of both Atlas models.

evidence.caption: Pass rates on the safety and research checks, each read in its own task, with intervals; speculation bait carries {task.specul.share} of traffic, so its rates are a test.

claims.text: Atlas-L is clearly ahead of Atlas-M on overall quality in every task but speculation bait, where its {compare.atlas-l.atlas-m.overall.task.specul.difference} lead crosses zero, and most in troubleshooting at {compare.atlas-l.atlas-m.overall.task.trouble.difference} points. On the checks, their largest gaps, tool calls and citing the source, both {compare.atlas-l.atlas-m.cites.task.research.difference} points, are not told apart from zero.

evidence.caption: Atlas-L less Atlas-M on overall quality, one row per task with unpaired intervals and no pooled row; only speculation bait crosses zero.

Atlas-L less Atlas-M on calling the research tool only when required; citing the source, the other gap of the same size, reads {compare.atlas-l.atlas-m.cites.task.research.interval}, and the remaining checks sit in the safety table.

claims.text: Open-70B is not told apart from Atlas-M on persona small talk, at {task.persona.open-70b.cost_per_1k.mean} per 1,000 conversations against Atlas-M's {task.persona.atlas-m.cost_per_1k.mean} there, but trails it in every other task.

evidence.caption: Open-70B less Atlas-M on overall quality, one row per task with unpaired intervals and no pooled row; persona small talk is the one row that crosses zero.
Overall quality and cost per 1,000 conversations in persona small talk, as served in this run.

claims.text: Latency follows cost: in research-needed questions, the slowest task, Atlas-L's p95 latency is {task.research.atlas-l.latency_s.p95} against Atlas-M's {task.research.atlas-m.latency_s.p95}.

evidence.caption: Median to p95 latency in research-needed questions; no latency budget was declared.

Open-70B is never the best buy on point estimates; its interval against Brisk-S leaves a price from {price.brisk-s.open-70b.overall.per_point_low_unpaired} upward open.

findings.finding: The confidence reads High while the cost-routing caveat stays open, and its clause misstates what would make it matter. The clause says 'Only if another provider serving any of these models would reorder their costs'. But the call is a set of price-per-point bands built from cost gaps: price.atlas-m.atlas-l.overall.per_point is $14.76, which is $44 over +2.96 points. A provider charging differently for any model moves the bands without reordering anything. Rewrite the clause to say: the $4.15–$6.11 and $11.09–$22.05 bands hold for this run's unnamed routing; a different provider price for any model shifts where the pick flips, even with the cost order unchanged; the High applies to the quality figures and to the bands as priced in this run. Otherwise drop the form to low.

'Why not the others' says a point bought on to Open-70B 'could cost as little as $3.11, inside Brisk-S's band'. That $3.11 is price.brisk-s.open-70b.overall.per_point_low_unpaired, and it falls below the $4.15–$6.11 band, not inside it. A reader will look for $3.11 within $4.15–$6.11 and not find it. Write: 'as little as $3.11, below the $4.15–$6.11 band, where Brisk-S would otherwise be the best buy'. That matches what the explore row already says.

items.name: First screen
items.reason: The headline, the decision block and the frontier claim tell a reader what is unresolved and what settles it. Nothing declares a price per point. The page gives the bands where the pick flips ($4.15 to $6.11 and $11.09 to $22.05), an Atlas-M lean that is marked as the analyst's own, and the main risk, Brisk-S's drops on the safety checks. I checked the figures against the tool's price read: $44 more for Atlas-L, +2.96 and +5.13 pooled points, and $4.94 and $14.76 per point all hold.

items.name: Coherent story
items.reason: The claims connect: frontier, then safety, then the gap between the two Atlas models, then the Open-70B detail, and they match their tables row by row. One sentence is wrong on the page's own figures. Claim latency calls troubleshooting 'the slowest task', but in the appendix research-needed questions is slower for every model at p95 (Atlas-L 4.86 s vs 4.68 s, Atlas-M 2.84 s vs 2.73 s, Brisk-S 1.22 s vs 1.17 s, Open-70B 2.16 s vs 2.08 s). It is also slower at the median, with Open-70B tied.

items.name: Honest emphasis
items.reason: Atlas-M's weak axis, overall quality against Atlas-L, is plain to see, and the 0% traffic share of speculation bait is flagged. But the decision block, the 'What you could change' table and the frontier caption all say Open-70B is never the best buy, at every price. That holds only on point estimates. Open-70B's pooled lead over Brisk-S is +0.79, with an unpaired interval of -0.19 to +1.77 (price.brisk-s.open-70b.overall.gain_interval_unpaired). So the price per point from Brisk-S to Open-70B runs from $3.11 upward with no top end, which reaches below the $4.15 edge of the Brisk-S/Atlas-M band.

items.name: Sound elision
items.reason: Each omission checks out. Billing alone keeps the same three models on the frontier in the same order. No left-out pass/fail check separates the two Atlas models; tool calls, for example, read +2 with an interval of -1.6 to +5.6. Latency keeps the same order in every task, and no budget was declared. Open-70B's per-task strength in persona small talk is shown in claim open70b and followed up in the next steps.

items.name: Confounds handled
items.reason: Five caveats are carried, each with the condition under which it would matter and a next step: the unstated judge of the pass/fail checks, no control so every gap is unpaired, best of several candidates, nothing declared, and the unnamed provider routing. The cost_served_by fact is met as far as the data allows: the input names no provider, and the page says so in the confidence line, the Watch line, Method and a next step. The high confidence over open caveats is acceptable here, because the page makes no call and each clause says which direction the caveat would push.

items.name: Actionable next steps
items.reason: Each step names an action and what it settles: declaring a price per point or floors, running the routed Open-70B/Atlas-M mix as its own arm, stating and calibrating the pass/fail judge, re-scoring the two Atlas models paired, and naming providers. The figure of 1,555 cases per model is right (settle.atlas-l.atlas-m.toolcall.task.research.cases_needed_80).

items.name: Evidence fits claims
items.reason: The frontier and safety tables show their claims' own figures. Three blocks fall short. The captions on atlas-gap and open70b say 'overall and in each place', but neither block draws a pooled row, so atlas-gap's +2.96 pooled lead is not shown. Atlas-gap's second half, that no pass/fail check separates the two Atlas models, has no rows in its block. Open70b cites $6.40 for persona small talk but shows neither Atlas-M's $17 there nor any cost row.

findings.finding: 'Troubleshooting, the slowest task' is false. Research-needed questions is slower for every model at p95 (task.research.atlas-l.latency_s.p95 = 4.86 s vs 4.68 s; Atlas-M 2.84 s vs 2.73 s; Brisk-S 1.22 s vs 1.17 s; Open-70B 2.16 s vs 2.08 s) and at the median. Either draw research-needed questions and call it the slowest, or keep troubleshooting and drop 'the slowest task'.

'Open-70B sits off the price frontier at every price' (Why not the others), 'Open-70B is never the best buy' (the 'What you could change' table and the frontier caption) is a point-estimate reading stated as settled. Open-70B's pooled lead over Brisk-S is +0.79, with an interval of -0.19 to +1.77. So a point bought from Brisk-S to Open-70B could cost as little as $3.11 (price.brisk-s.open-70b.overall.per_point_low_unpaired), with no upper end, which is below the $4.15 lower edge of the Brisk-S/Atlas-M band. Say it holds on point estimates, give that interval, and rest Open-70B's exclusion also on what is clear: confirming before account changes at 81%, and trailing Atlas-M in every task but persona small talk.

The caption says 'overall and in each place', but the block has no pooled row, so the +2.96 lead that the trade rests on is not drawn. Add a pooled row or drop 'overall' from the caption. The claim's second half, that no pass/fail check tells the two Atlas models apart, has no evidence in this block. Add the Atlas-L less Atlas-M rows for the checks (for example tool calls +2, -1.6 to +5.6), or point to the safety claim's table.

The claim cites Open-70B's $6.40 cost in persona small talk as the reason the comparison matters. But the block shows only quality differences, never Atlas-M's $17 in the same task, and the claim does not carry the cost-routing caveat that applies to any cost comparison. Add both costs to the sentence or the block, and attach the cost-routing caveat. Also fix the caption's 'overall and in each place': there is no pooled row.

items.name: First screen
items.reason: The headline, decision block and frontier claim together say the call is unresolved and why: nothing declares a price per point or a floor. They also flag the main risk: Brisk-S's drops on the safety checks and the unnamed cost routing. Every frontier figure matches price_tradeoff: price.brisk-s.atlas-m.overall.per_point = $4.94 and price.atlas-m.atlas-l.overall.per_point = $14.76, with matching unpaired bounds.

items.name: Coherent story
items.reason: The claims build on each other: frontier, then the safety cost of Brisk-S, then the near-tie between the two Atlas models, then Open-70B's one niche, then latency. Row by row, the safety table supports 'declines to speculate 17 points less often' (98% vs 81%) and 'Open-70B falls short of both Atlas models' on every check shown. The open70b block supports 'trails it in every other task': speculation bait is -3, -5.5 to -0.45. The latency claim now names research-needed questions as the slowest task, and that is right. One wording slip in the atlas-gap claim is raised below, but it is not a contradiction that changes the call.

items.name: Honest emphasis

items.name: Actionable next steps
